text:
maria: Heads-up — after the kernel route change last night we see a fine-grained OOM surge on a subset of kv-heavy requests. Not full cluster outage but p50 p99 memory climbs and a handful of prefill-heavy requests get killed.

jonathan: Ugh. Which kernel change? the attention tiling swap?

sam: Yes the tiling + small-batch kernel path. It reduced latency for most small requests but looks like it increased workspace fragmentation in our slab pools.

lee: Can we repro with a focused microbench? low-entropy prompt + long prefill sequence? I can throw a local janky runner against a dev GPU.

maria: I ran a short sim against the kv-cache traces (last 24h). Repro steps and diff are below. Repro is deterministic if you force path selection to `tiling_small_batch`.

maria: ```
# repro: run-local with kernel_override=tiling_small_batch
./run_gbench --trace=kv_traces/kv_hot_20260317.json --kernel=tiling_small_batch --prefill=true --max-seq=1024
# outputs: OOM in allocator::alloc_slab at 0x7f...
```

sam: Interesting. My profiler snapshot shows many small free fragments in the KV slab arena after decode churn. Prefill creates big KV entries, decode touches them and writes small deltas -> fragmentation.

jonathan: Do we have a recent allocator histogram? slab utilization / fragmentation %?

maria: Quick numbers from the run: total gpu mem 48GB, kv-slab reserved 18GB, active kv usage 14.2GB, fragmentation (estimated) 2.7GB (19%). Prefill-only runs show fragmentation ~8-9%, but prefill+decode jumps to ~19%.

lee: So decode path is causing non-coalescing frees. Likely different allocation size classes between prefill and decode. If prefill uses large contiguous blocks and decode allocates many small buffers we'll get internal fragmentation.

sam: Agreed. Two immediate mitigations: 1) enforce per-request KV cap (soft cap) to limit decode-resident allocations; 2) coalesce small frees into a recycler bucket to avoid returning them to the slab freelist and causing fragmentation.

maria: I prototyped a per-request cap at 256MB for KV and re-ran. Result: peak fragmentation drops to ~11% and no OOMs in the same runs. Latency impact negligible for non-pathological requests.

jonathan: Nice. Can you paste the config diff you used?

maria: ```
# runtime config snippet
kv_cache: 
  per_request_soft_cap_bytes: 268435456  # 256MB
  eviction_policy: LRU_SEGMENTED
  prefill_bias: true
  small_alloc_recycler_enable: false  # prev setting

allocator: 
  slab_slab_size_bytes: 134217728  # 128MB slabs
  small_alloc_bucket_threshold: 4096
```

lee: That helps, but small_alloc_recycler_enable=false was the old behavior. We should flip it to true and tune the bucket threshold to absorb decode churn.

sam: I added a quick recycler and ran the same sim with `small_alloc_recycler_enable=true` and `small_alloc_bucket_threshold=8192`. Fragmentation went down to 7.3% and p99 memory stable. CPU overhead small.

maria: Good. Any risk to latency due to extra memcpy or bucket management?

sam: Measured ~+0.2ms on decode path for the worst-case small-allocation hot loop — within our SLO.

jonathan: We should also consider adaptive prefill throttling: when fragmentation crosses X% or OOM risk > Y, reduce aggressive prefill size per request. That keeps throughput while avoiding OOM spikes.

lee: Agreed. Also kernel selector could incorporate fragmentation signals: avoid tiling_small_batch when slab fragmentation > threshold; route to kernel version that uses larger contiguous work segments. That ties kernel selection to allocator health.

maria: I sketched a fallback policy: if (fragmentation_ratio > 0.12 AND concurrent_prefill_requests > 8) then prefer `legacy_batch` kernel. Quick sim shows this avoids the OOMs and keeps average latency within 5% of baseline.

jonathan: Nice. We need to be careful with rollout: toggling kernel by condition might hide underlying bug. But as a short-term mitigation it's good. Add telemetry to alert if fallback engages more than 1% of requests for >10m.

maria: I'll add metrics: `allocator.frag_ratio`, `kv.prefill_count`, `kernel.fallback_rate`. Also adding a histogram of freed-size distribution to detect drift in alloc size mix.

sam: Action items I can take today: 1) land small_alloc_recycler with bucket tuning (8192 initial), 2) add per-request KV soft cap config and default 256MB, 3) add metric for freed-size histogram.

lee: I'll wire the kernel selector to the frag metric behind a flag and run canary on dedicated nodes.

jonathan: Let's also run a controlled stress test with mixed prefill/decode traces: 10k requests over 30m, varying prefill lengths and decode churn. Capture allocator traces + nvprof. Post results to thread.

maria: Ran a small canary already: with recycler + soft cap + selector flag off, canary on 4 dev nodes passed with no OOMs for 2h. Will run the 30m stress tomorrow.

infra-bot: deploy: canary build 2026.03.17-rc4 started on dev-pool-3 (4 nodes). Logs: /builds/2026.03.17-rc4/logs

maria: Thanks. If the larger stress passes, let's cut a patch for the recycler + config, and enable selector flag on dedicated tier only initially.

jonathan: Hold a short sync after the stress test to decide defaults and rollout plan. Good work team :thumbsup:
